Tomato.name: Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
Tomato.symptoms: Concentric dark brown rings on older leaves forming a 'target board' pattern, yellow halo around lesions, stem cankers.

weather_triggers.high_risk_condition: Frequent rainfall alternating with warm sunny days, extended leaf wetness (> 8 hours).

organic_remedies: Spray Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) or 10,000 ppm Cold-pressed Neem Oil @ 3-5 ml/liter water.
Foliar application of bio-fungicide Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5g/liter water during morning hours.
Prune infected lower foliage up to 1 foot above soil surface to stop soil-borne fungal splash.
cultural_prevention: Maintain proper plant spacing (60 x 45 cm) for airflow.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; use drip irrigation to prevent wetting foliage.
Mulch soil around plants with straw to prevent fungal spores in soil splashing onto leaves.
Tomato.hazard_warning: Avoid indiscriminate use of Mancozeb or Copper Oxychloride without protective gear. Never spray when honeybees or pollinators are actively foraging.

Tomato.name: Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) via Whiteflies
Tomato.symptoms: Upward curling, puckering, and crinkling of leaf margins, stunted plant growth, bushy appearance, reduced flowering.

weather_triggers.high_risk_condition: Dry, hot weather with low wind speed favoring whitefly vector multiplication.

organic_remedies: Install Yellow Sticky Traps @ 15-20 traps per acre at crop canopy height to capture adult whiteflies.
Spray 2% Neem oil solution combined with 1 ml liquid soap per liter as an emulsifier.
Spray Beauveria bassiana or Verticillium lecanii bio-agent @ 5g/liter water in evening.
cultural_prevention: Erect 2 rows of barrier crops like Maize, Bajra, or Sorghum around the tomato plot 30 days before transplanting.
Rogue out and destroy infected viral plants immediately away from the field.
Tomato.hazard_warning: Viral diseases cannot be cured with chemical fungicides. Do not waste money spraying fungicides for virus infections.

Paddy (Rice).name: Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae)
Paddy (Rice).symptoms: Spindle or diamond-shaped lesions with gray/white centers and brownish margins on leaves, neck blast causing empty panicles.

weather_triggers.high_risk_condition: Overcast days, nighttime dew condensation, cool night temperatures, excessive nitrogen fertilizer.

organic_remedies: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg of seed before sowing.
Foliar spray of 5% raw cow urine extract fermented with crushed neem leaves.
Apply Silica-rich amendments (e.g., rice husk ash) to strengthen plant epidermal cell walls.
cultural_prevention: Split nitrogenous fertilizer application into 3-4 doses; avoid excessive urea.
Maintain optimal water level (2-3 cm) in fields during tillering stage.
Paddy (Rice).hazard_warning: Tricyclazole should only be used as a last resort in severe outbreaks. Overuse leads to resistance and chemical residue in food grain.

Paddy (Rice).name: Yellow Stem Borer (Scirpophaga incertulas)
Paddy (Rice).symptoms: Drying of central tiller leading to 'dead heart' in vegetative phase; empty white panicles ('white head') during reproductive phase.

weather_triggers.high_risk_condition: Warm humid conditions during active tillering with low wind.

organic_remedies: Set up Pheromone traps with 'Scirpolure' lures @ 5-8 traps/acre for monitoring and mass trapping.
Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma japonicum @ 40,000 to 50,000 parasites/acre at weekly intervals.
Clip seedling leaf tips before transplanting to eliminate egg masses.
cultural_prevention: Install 'T' shaped bird perches @ 10-15 per acre to invite insectivorous birds.
Submerge fields for 24-48 hours after harvest to kill diapausing larvae in stubbles.
Paddy (Rice).hazard_warning: Granular carbofuran or chlorpyrifos severely degrades aquatic life and groundwater in wetlands. Prohibited near fish habitats.

Cotton.name: Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella)
Cotton.symptoms: Rosetted flowers that fail to open, entry holes on green bolls sealed with excreta, stained lint and damaged seeds inside bolls.

weather_triggers.high_risk_condition: Continuous warm, cloudy weather during squaring and boll formation.

organic_remedies: Install Gossyplure pheromone traps @ 8-10 traps/acre for mass male moth trapping.
Spray Neem oil (1500 ppm) @ 5 ml/liter water at 45 and 60 days after sowing.
Release Trichogramma bactrae @ 60,000/acre at weekly intervals starting from 40 DAS.
cultural_prevention: Plant non-Bt cotton refuge crop along borders.
Avoid extended crop cultivation beyond 150 days; terminate crop by January to break pest lifecycle.
Cotton.hazard_warning: Overuse of synthetic pyrethroids has created severe pesticide resistance and secondary resurgence of whiteflies.

Potato.name: Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans)
Potato.symptoms: Water-soaked irregular black/purplish lesions on leaf tips and margins, white cottony fungal growth on leaf undersides in high humidity, rotting tubers.

weather_triggers.high_risk_condition: Persistent foggy/cloudy weather, cold night temperatures with heavy morning dew, RH > 90% for 48 consecutive hours.

organic_remedies: Prophylactic spray of Trichoderma viride @ 5g/liter or fermented butter milk (chaas) mixed with copper vessel extract (traditional recipe).
Spray potassium phosphite or bio-formulations containing Bacillus subtilis @ 3g/liter.
cultural_prevention: Ensure proper earthing-up so tubers are deeply covered with soil to prevent spore penetration.
Potato.hazard_warning: Late Blight can destroy an entire field within 48-72 hours. Proactive prevention before rain is critical.

Wheat.name: Stripe / Yellow Rust (Puccinia striiformis)
Wheat.symptoms: Yellow powder stripes parallel to leaf veins that leave yellow residue when touched with fingers.

weather_triggers.high_risk_condition: Cool, humid weather with intermittent drizzles in Northern/North-Western plains.

organic_remedies: Spray 5% sour buttermilk (3-4 days old fermented curd whey) diluted with water.
Foliar application of bio-agent Ampelomyces quisqualis or Trichoderma harzianum @ 5g/liter.
cultural_prevention: Sow resistant wheat varieties recommended for the agro-climatic zone (e.g., HD-2967, DBW-187).
Timely sowing in November to escape late season rust pressure.
Wheat.hazard_warning: Do not mix chemical fungicides with bio-agents; bio-agents will be killed by chemical fungicides.
